page: Amazon Web Services r8gn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors. It features 64 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz on the arm64 architecture, with 1.0 thread per core. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, but it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier capabilities in memory bandwidth, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 7394.84 GB/sec and large block uncached speeds at 479.59 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is strong, as evidenced by top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core, Passmark CPU physics, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling in the average range. The instance also exhibits a performance tradeoff in low-parameter LLM text generation, scoring in the bottom 10% for a small 135M model, though it maintains strong text generation speeds for medium and large models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r8gn.16xlarge offers high memory density and exceptional memory bandwidth relative to its ARM-based hardware profile, making it highly efficient for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of x86 licensing. It is highly optimized for network and EBS throughput. This profile is best suited for memory-intensive applications, high-throughput database operations, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and large-scale software compilation.
